keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1992-1995 shape is 147,904 km2 against the infobox 102,173 km2 (body 102,350; ratio 1.45). The gazetteer shows it holds 173 cells (about 43,750 km2) that the 1996 shape does not - 116 cells in Bosnia and Herzegovina and 55 in Croatia - the Serb-held Republika Srpska and Krajina, which the page says were separate entities that received 'unofficial aid'. The 1996 outline is the right shape for 1992-1995; the two Serb entities have their own dossiers (republika-srpska, republic-of-serbian-krajina).

101,815 km2 against the infobox 102,173 km2 (ratio 1.00): Serbia with Kosovo and Vojvodina, and Montenegro. Cliopatria runs the shape to 1999; Kosovo leaves Belgrade's control in June 1999 (ledger), so the Kosovo cells (about 10,400 km2) drop out in the same year. Prevlaka (Croatian peninsula held by Yugoslav forces) is not on the pages opened.

correction.text: shape unchanged, but it holds 2000-2006 (to the end of the State Union in June 2006, not 2005): Serbia without Kosovo, and Montenegro

keyframe_review.note: 90,685 km2 (infobox 102,173 km2 with Kosovo; ratio 0.89, the difference being Kosovo, about 10,900 km2). Cliopatria ends the row in 2005 and starts the Republic of Serbia and Montenegro rows in 2006, but Montenegro declared independence on 3 June 2006 and Serbia followed on 5 June 2006 ('effectively dissolving the union'), so 2006 is a hand-over year.

region.text: Serbia and Montenegro, 'established on 27 April 1992 as a federation'

ledger.note: 27 April 1992: Serbia and Montenegro proclaim the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. It 'claimed to continue the international legal personality and United Nations membership' of the SFR Yugoslavia; the UN did not accept this. Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina were 'separate entities' given unofficial aid.

July 1998: the Kosovo Liberation Army holds ground. The war page dates the war to 28 February 1998 - 11 June 1999; the Yugoslav army and Serbian police began an operation against the KLA on 1 June 1998, the KLA 'captured Orahovac in mid-July' and Yugoslav counter-offensives ran into August. The page does not outline the KLA-held zone.

June 1999: the Kosovo War ends. 'The war ended with the Kumanovo Agreement, signed on 9 June 1999'; infobox end 11 June 1999; NATO bombing ran 24 March - 11 June 1999 and KFOR 'began entering Kosovo' on 12 June.

June 1999: Kosovo passes under UN administration. 'In June 1999, Kosovo became an entity under interim international administration'; UNSCR 1244 'guaranteed economic and political separation of Kosovo from the FR Yugoslavia' and the withdrawal of Yugoslav units; the Kosovo War page notes 'No de jure changes to Yugoslav borders'.
4 February 2003: the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia becomes the State Union of Serbia and Montenegro; colour and dossier continue.

3 June 2006: Montenegro declares independence. The referendum of 21 May 2006 passed with '55.5% of voters' for independence, 'narrowly above the 55% threshold'; the parliament 'formally declared independence on 3 June 2006'.

region.text: the State Union of Serbia and Montenegro, ended when Serbia followed Montenegro

ledger.note: 5 June 2006: Serbia's parliament 'did the same, effectively dissolving the union'; the land passes to the independent republics of Serbia and Montenegro (Kosovo having been under UN administration since 1999).

wars.name: Kosovo War
wars.outcome: NATO bombing (24 March - 11 June 1999) and the Kumanovo Agreement of 9 June 1999 ended the war; Yugoslav forces left and Kosovo passed to UN administration, with 'no de jure changes to Yugoslav borders' under UNSCR 1244.

certainty.note: The borders of Serbia and Montenegro are the former republic and state boundaries. Exceptions: Kosovo in 1998-1999 (fighting zone, soft) and the unsettled Prevlaka frontier with Croatia (not described on the pages opened).

notes:
Serbia-Montenegro, written by eu-22-g on 2026-11-01 from the Serbia and Montenegro and Kosovo War pages (two pages, the budget). The Cliopatria row is one state under two names, the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia (1992-2003) and the State Union of Serbia and Montenegro (2003-2006); no split is needed, the change is a rename event.

Cliopatria's 1992-1995 shape holds the Serb-held parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina (116 cells) and Croatia (55 cells), which belong to republika-srpska and republic-of-serbian-krajina (dossiers exist); the verdict removes them. The shape is accepted for 1996-1999 and for 2000-2005 without Kosovo.

Not on the pages opened: Prevlaka (Croatian peninsula held by Yugoslav forces), the Yugoslav Army's withdrawal date from the Croatian and Bosnian fronts, the UN Resolution 777 date, and the date of UNSCR 1244 (10 June 1999 is not given on the Kosovo War page; the ledger says June 1999). Kosovo's own dossier (eu-22) records the UN administration and the 2008 declaration. The successors montenegro and republic-of-serbia are Cliopatria rows from 2006; the end year 2006 makes that a hand-over year in which both the union and its successors may be drawn.

Rulers: the page lists heads of state with years only; Marović held the State Union's own presidency from 2003.
